about.text: Butter churned from cream that has first been soured with lactic acid bacteria, giving it a fuller, slightly tangy taste and the aroma of diacetyl. Sold in Germany as Sauerrahmbutter.

picture.file: Antoine Vollon - Mound of Butter - National Gallery of Art.jpg
picture.author: Antoine Vollon

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: The culture sours the cream while its fat crystallises in the ripening tank, and the aroma strains make diacetyl. That gives the butter its fuller, buttery smell, and the acid protects it against unwanted microbes.

microbes.name: Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis biovar diacetylactis

steps.note: Soured during the ripening, in summer at 20 °C for about 5 h.
In the summer programme the cream is cooled at about 22 °SH.
